newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends stronger on large export deals.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends stronger on large export deals.

text.p: The won closed higher versus the dollar on Thursday on the back of unexpectedly large demand in the late session, traders said.
Heavy month-end export deals, coupled with inflow of foreign loans, sparked active dollar selling, they said.
The won ended at 826.40 after trading in a wide range of 826.30 to 830.50. It opened at 830.00.

"Shortage of the won in the money market is pressuring the dollar," said one dealer. "Banks don't believe the liquidity situation will get any better early next month and this is expected to dampen the sentiment."
Traders said the won was likely to remain firm at the current level on Friday in a range of 825 to 828.
The central bank set the base mid-rate for Friday at 828.90 against today's 831.30.
